newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka fines two Germans for reptile smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka fines two Germans for reptile smuggling.

text.p: Two Germans were fined a total of 60,000 rupees ($1,050) by a Sri Lankan court on Monday for trying to take more than 50 reptiles out of the country without a permit, police said.

The two Germans were stopped late on Saturday as they drove towards the airport in a van loaded with six boxes which contained live lizards, frogs and two vipers, police in the town of Athurugiriya, 20 km (12 miles) south of Colombo, said.
"There were a total of 58 live animals packed into the boxes," a police officer told Reuters. The Germans were not identified.
The animals were handed over to officials from the Colombo zoo to be released into their natural environment, he said.
Sri Lankan law prohibits the export of live wild animals without a permit from the Department of Wildlife Conservation.
